subject: occu() function is failing with a huge data set. ideas?

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: occu() function is failing with a huge data set. ideas?
parts:
Dear all,
 I have a large occupancy data set, 6144 sites and 5 replicates.  When I run the models through occu() in unmarked they simply fail. The estimates never deviate much from the starting values. I tried alternative algorithms in optim() and they all fail too.  On the other hand the models seem to fit well using nlm() with my own likelihood function.  I'm curious if anyone has seen this before and/or if anyone has ideas for how to resolve this... I show some evidence of things below. 
Thanks a lot for any ideas!
andy


(1) Here is a simply glm using the covariate Freq and Freq^2:

summary( glm(y~Freq+I(Freq^2), data.frame(data), family="binomial")  )

Call:
glm(formula = y ~ Freq + I(Freq^2), family = "binomial", data = data.frame(data))

Deviance Residuals:
    Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
-0.7656  -0.4897  -0.1112  -0.0014   4.0468 

Coefficients:
            Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)   
(Intercept) -4.38099    0.09960  -43.98   <2e-16 ***
Freq        -4.16516    0.13510  -30.83   <2e-16 ***
I(Freq^2)   -1.31280    0.04306  -30.48   <2e-16 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 

These results are correct. There is a very strong quadratic response of Freq.


(2)  Here is the occu() result:

>
>  occu(~Freq + I(Freq^2) ~1, umf , method="Nelder-Mead", start  = c( 0.3, -3.7, -4.13, -1.28 ) ) 

Call:
occu(formula = ~Freq + I(Freq^2) ~ 1, data = umf, starts = c(0.3,
    -3.7, -4.13, -1.28), method = "Nelder-Mead")

Occupancy:
 Estimate     SE     z   P(>|z|)
    -1.11 0.0353 -31.5 3.02e-217

Detection:
            Estimate     SE       z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)  -0.6086 0.0475 -12.809 1.47e-37
Freq         -0.0197 0.0213  -0.926 3.54e-01
I(Freq^2)    -0.0754 0.0146  -5.177 2.25e-07

AIC: 14348.65

Note that the model seems to have been fitted successfully but the results are non-sense.  The parameters are nowhere near the correct values. 


(3) I wrote my own likelihood function to confirm this and it gives the correct answer (See below)

> lik<- function(parm, y, X){
+
+
+ psi<- plogis(parm[1])
+ p<- plogis(parm[2] + parm[3]*X[,1] + parm[4]*X[,2] )
+
+ lik<- log(
+ dbinom(y, 5, p)*psi + as.numeric(y==0)*(1-psi) )
+
+ -1*sum(lik)
+
+
+ }
>
> y<- as.matrix(dat[,3:7])
> y<- apply(y,1,sum)
>
> Hour<- as.matrix(Sampling.covs[,"Hour"] -12)/6
> Freq=(as.matrix(Sampling.covs[,"Freq"])-12000)/4000
>  X<- cbind(Freq, Freq^2, Hour, Hour^2)
> nlm(lik,c(0,0,0,0 ), y=y,X=X, hessian=TRUE)
$minimum
[1] 3696.258

$estimate
[1]  0.3006613 -3.7241844 -4.1311890 -1.2820000

$gradient
[1] -0.0003587593 -0.0003785932  0.0008320279 -0.0023037848

$hessian
          [,1]       [,2]       [,3]      [,4]
[1,]  415.8204   344.4579  -536.4217  1098.494
[2,]  344.4579  1230.9270 -1880.0170  3441.364
[3,] -536.4217 -1880.0170  3441.1893 -6956.080
[4,] 1098.4936  3441.3641 -6956.0801 15156.649

$code
[1] 1

$iterations
[1] 24

parts:
hey Richard,
 see attached. Also you can that with:

 load("umf.RData")
occu(~Freq + I(Freq^2) ~1, umf , method="Nelder-Mead", start  = c( 0.3, -3.7, -4.13, -1.28 ) )

FWIW I edited the occu() function to use nlm() instead of optim() and I get the SAME failure result. I suspect therefore that the problem is related to the observation level likelihood formulation and some numerical problems associated with small numbers...
